title: Temporary & Permanent Differences
description: Distinguish temporary differences that reverse in future periods from permanent differences.
html:
Temporary differences

Temporary differences arise when the financial reporting carrying amount of an asset or liability differs from its tax basis in a way that can affect future taxable or deductible amounts.

The key idea is that the tax effect reverses in future periods.

Example — Different depreciation timing

Financial reporting and tax reporting may use different depreciation patterns.

This can cause book income and taxable income to differ today.

But the timing difference can reverse over the life of the asset.

Permanent differences

Permanent differences affect book income or taxable income but do not reverse in future periods.

Temporary

Timing difference

Future reversal

Can create deferred taxes

Permanent

No future reversal

Does not create a deferred tax asset or liability

Critical distinction

Temporary → think future tax consequence.

Permanent → there is no future reversal of that difference.

quiz.prompt: Which statement best describes a temporary difference?

choices.text: A difference that can create future taxable or deductible amounts
A difference that can never affect future periods
A difference that always increases cash

quiz.explanation: Temporary differences involve differences between book carrying amounts and tax bases that can result in future taxable or deductible amounts.
